first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the completion decline and has previously improved completion, time-to-value, early adoption, and SMB activation. This is more aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose acquisition gains came with materially worse 30-day retention. Verify the onboarding and activation-message source records before committing because both current declines could plausibly be the primary constraint.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has confirmed durable evidence of +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention; prior evidence also links signup simplification to stronger SMB activation. This offers the strongest sustainable-revenue path while avoiding promotional pricing's documented retention harm. Activation messaging remains a credible follow-up if activation does not recover sufficiently after onboarding friction is reduced.

final2.rationale: Given the acute, doubled churn pressure among price-sensitive SMB accounts after the deeper competitor cut, run a tightly targeted, small guarded promotional-pricing test for that at-risk segment only. Prior evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift in this segment, but also shows material 30-day retention harm; do not broaden the offer without confirming that retained qualified revenue improves after the promotion ends.
